 By Fielding Buck | fbuck@scng.com PUBLISHED: November 19, 2026 at 1:28 PM PST | UPDATED: November 20, 2026 at 3:04 PM PST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... East Coast meets West Coast at Yaamava’ Resort & Casino near Highland, which has debuted a new holiday display by Martha Stewart.
 It’s called Martha’s Forest of Wonder. It was created by Stewart and Kevin Sharkey, a longtime executive of her lifestyle brand, Martha Stewart Living, working long-distance with Jerry Bowlen, the resort’s director of hospitality horticulture, and his team.
 Stewart, who lives in the Hudson Valley north of New York City, wanted the project to reflect her enthusiasm for nature as well as California’s wildlife, Sharkey said in an interview. To add a touch of seasonal whimsy, some of the animals have been bedazzled with rhinestones or draped with gold leaf.
 Several of the scenes have CGI animation depicting snow falling on winter landscapes.

 Expand 
 Sharkey said Stewart was involved in storyboarding the project. She saw the results on her first visit to the resort for the display’s formal launch on Wednesday, Nov. 18.
 Martha’s Forest of Wonder unfolds in several scenes through the resort. Here are some of the highlights.
 The second-floor entrance from the parking structure most visitors use features pictures of animals in a long hallway leading to the casino. There are also selfie stations, one with two black bears and the other a forest panorama.
 The ground-floor entrance where the casino shuttles run has a scene representing Stewart’s Bedford Farm in the Hudson Valley.
 The high rollers room has a fox and raccoon sitting under Christmas trees surrounded by giant red mushrooms.
 Martha Stewart makes Inland Empire debut at Yaamava’ Resort & Casino 
 There are more animals and trees at the base of the escalators to the second floor of the casino.
 A sleigh supplied by Stewart from her collection is parked near the entrance to the hotel, which has two towering trees in its lobby.
 Families looking for holiday magic should be aware that Yaamava’ is an age 21 and older property.
 The Yuhaaviatam of San Manuel Nation, which owns the resort, acquired the Mission Inn Hotel & Spa in Riverside earlier this year, meaning the tribe now has a hand in two major holiday displays. Yaamava’ will be providing shuttle service to downtown Riverside and the Mission Inn Hotel & Spa Festival of Lights , which will run Nov. 21-Dec. 31. Shuttles are open to the public as well as Yaamava’ hotel guests, according to Visit Riverside, the city’s tourism organization. Passengers must be 21 and older.
 Information: yaamava.com , riversideca.gov/fol
